Subject: ACME: Post-call TCO recap & next steps (token economics + levers)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the time today — appreciate you walking us through the production workload and the cost constraints you're operating under. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: unpredictable token spend and a handful of high-traffic endpoints that spike latency/cost during batch runs.
- Goal: get to a predictable $/monthly inference spend within a 10% variance, and reduce per-request latency for 95th pctile to <350ms.

Key cost drivers we discussed
- Model size & token footprint: average request = 820 input tokens, expected output ~120 tokens.
- QPS patterns: 50 steady QPS, spikes to 300 for 10-15min windows.
- Lack of prefix caching + no batching today increases per-token compute.

Recommended levers and rough TCO impact (see attached spreadsheet for math)
1) Prefix/KV caching: for repeat prompts we expect 20-40% token compute reduction on common routes.
2) Adaptive batching (latency-aware): combine small requests during low-latency windows - estimated 15-25% unit-cost savings without affecting P95 if we keep max latency budget for those routes.
3) Quantized model variant for bulk/rerank routes: ~30-50% GPU utilization improvement on non-critical routes.
4) Model routing by SLA: route high-priority UI calls to lower-latency (higher-cost) pool, bulk jobs to quantized/dedicated pools.

Preliminary numbers (monthly projection, baseline vs with levers) - see ACME_TCO_summary_20270430.xlsx for details:
- Baseline: $85k/month
- With caching + batching + quantization + routing: $53k-60k/month (30-38% savings)

Risks & open questions
- Procurement/contract constraints around model quantization and data residency.
- SLA tolerance for batched routes - need to confirm which endpoints can accept a few extra ms.
- Security questionnaire items (we can provide SOC2 artifacts; Marissa will lead).

Suggested next steps
1) I’ll share the detailed TCO workbook (attached).
2) Marissa to send the SOC2 + security checklist items you flagged.
3) Quick scoping call with Tom (finance) to validate procurement and target monthly budget (30 minutes).
4) Pilot: 4-6 week pilot on one high-volume endpoint (batch/caching + quantized variant).

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min finance scoping call next week? We’re available Monday/Tuesday 9-11am PT or Wednesday 2-4pm PT.

Thanks again - happy to adjust any of the assumptions in the sheet.

Best,
Ben Carter

- Procurement: we prefer a 12-month committed spend with a quarterly reconciliation clause. Procurement will want to review terms in the PDF.
